reason: The passage demonstrates collaboration between leaders and people on both sides of the narrative. On the Egyptian side, Pharaoh actively takes his people (צְבָאוֹ/his army) with him in pursuing the Israelites, as shown in 'וַיֶּאְסֹר אֶת־ רִכְבּוֹ וְאֶת־ עַמּוֹ לָקַח עִמּוֹ' ('he made ready his chariot and took his people with him'). On the Israelite side, despite the people's initial fear and complaint, they ultimately respond to Moses' leadership instruction ('אַל־ תִּירָאוּ הִֽתְיַצְבוּ וּרְאוּ אֶת־ יְשׁוּעַ֣ת יְהוָה' - 'Fear not, stand firm and see the salvation of the Lord'), and they collectively cross through the sea together. The narrative shows coordinated action between leaders and their people toward survival and escape.
